newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut demands death for official's murderers.
newsitem.headline: Beirut demands death for official's murderers.

text.p: A Lebanese prosecutor on Tuesday demanded the death penalty for four Beirut gang members for involvement in the killing of a Finance Ministry official tied to a multi-million dollar fraud case.

Prosecutor-general Tarabey Rahmeh demanded in an indictment the death penalty for Mohammad Harmoush for killing Ra'afat Sleiman, Antoine Tayyar for instigating the official's murder and Fouad Mousalli and Hisham Amloush for involvement in it.
Sleiman, whose mutilated body was found by police near a north Lebanon village on Sunday, has been at the centre of the fraud case that has caused a sensation in Lebanon.

In October, a prosecutor charged Sleiman, Tayyar, Mousalli's father Farid who was killed by police last month, and three other men with forging revenue stamps and selling for private gain genuine stamps supplied by the ministry.
The indictment had said the embezzled amount totalled 15 billion Lebanese pounds ($9.7 million) but acting finance minister Fouad Siniora last month said it amounted to 3.8 billion pounds.
Of the four charged, only Amloush is at large. All are Lebanese except Mousalli, who is Palestinian. No date has been set for their trial.
Sleiman, who was responsible for the sale of the stamps at the Finance Ministry, was buried in his home village in eastern Lebanon on Tuesday.
On Saturday, a military prosecutor ordered the arrest of a policeman for killing Farid Mousalli. Police had said last month Mousalli died in an exchange of fire with police trying to arrest him.
